title: Historical format
description: The top-level record tying together everything that defines one historical format. A format is mostly a set of REFERENCES into the shared datasets (banlists, pools, rule profiles); it should contain as little inline data as possible so that shared facts are stored exactly once.

id.description: Chronologically sortable id, e.g. 2005-04-goat. Must match the directory name formats/<id>/.

start.description: First day the format's defining conditions held (usually a banlist effective date).

end.description: Last day, if known. null while unresearched.

snapshot.description: The single representative date used for cutoff calculations (card pool, errata applicability). Usually the date of the format's defining event or the community-accepted reference point.

previous.description: Format id of the predecessor. May name a format not yet in the repository; the validator warns (not fails) on unresolved ids.

banlist.description: id of a banlist snapshot in data/banlists/.

card_pool.description: id of a pool definition in data/pools/.

rule_profile.description: id of a rule profile in data/rule-profiles/.

errata_policy.description: computed: tooling selects every erratum whose change post-dates this format's snapshot and applies the historical version. none: format explicitly opts out of historical card overrides.

errata_overrides.description: How this format resolves historical card behaviour beyond what each erratum record's chronology decides on its own. Per-card include/exclude entries are adjudications of last resort; the two policies below express, once and with sources, the standing decisions that would otherwise become giant hand-maintained lists.

include.description: erratum ids whose BASELINE historical version applies in this format regardless of (missing) chronology. A per-card adjudication: the validator reports entries that computed selection already agrees with (removable) and entries that contradict it (documented deviations).

exclude.description: erratum ids this format deliberately does NOT substitute, keeping the modern implementation. Document why in the format notes.

reference_parity.description: This format is DEFINED by reproducing an existing reference implementation, so it substitutes the upstream historical version of every card THE REFERENCE ITSELF represents by one. Membership is provenance-based, not 'every card that happens to have an upstream variant': `provenance_source` names the source id a record must cite to count as part of the reference. That matters because upstream ships historical variants for cards its own list does not use (Mind Crush, Ultimate Offering), and substituting those would break parity. Replaces a per-card include list with one sourced statement; where our own researched chronology disagrees with the reference (it would pick the modern card, or the record is cosmetic), the validator warns per card so the divergence stays visible instead of hiding inside a list.

reference_id.description: Stable slug identifying WHICH reference implementation/list this format reproduces (e.g. 'project-ignis-goat') - distinct from provenance_source, which is WHERE a record's assertion about that reference comes from. `provenance_source` names an entire pinned source (e.g. the whole ignis-lflists repository), which can host more than one reference list; `reference_id` disambiguates which one. When a v2 erratum's own `reference_identities[]` carries an entry whose `reference_id` matches this value, that EXACT entry is used in preference to the structural parity walk (docs/research/erratum-v2-representation-gaps.md). Optional for backward compatibility: a format with no `reference_id` uses only the existing provenance-membership + structural-walk behaviour, unaffected by this field.

provenance_source.description: Source id that marks a record as part of the reference implementation (e.g. 'ignis-lflists'). Records not citing it fall through to ordinary computed selection. Omit to treat every record with a historical implementation as part of the reference.

unresolved_policy.description: What this format does when a record's chronology is genuinely ambiguous at its snapshot. WITHOUT this, ambiguity is a hard error (the fail-safe default): selection never guesses. WITH it, the format states one sourced decision and the validator names every card it was applied to, so the choice is explicit and auditable rather than silent.

choice.description: modern: keep the modern implementation (conservative — claims no unproven historical behaviour). historical: use the baseline historical implementation.

relevant_products.description: Set/product codes (matching data/releases/) that frame this format, e.g. the last legal set.
